2608.30041.title: Reachability-Based Capability Confinement for LLM Agents under Indirect Prompt Injection
2608.30041.paper_summary: Large language model agents place outputs from external skills into their execution context, allowing attacker-controlled data to influence later privileged actions. Existing defenses mainly classify untrusted content or authorize proposed operations. They do not directly address how an agent's future authority should change once untrusted data enters its state. We present SkillGuard, a harness-level enforcement layer that treats this event as contamination and restricts future capabilities to disconnect the resulting state from deployer-defined forbidden states. Given sound skill summaries and policies, SkillGuard represents security-relevant transitions with a Skill Impact Graph, specifies admissible control over skill parameters via steerability signatures, and mediates invocations with an inline reference monitor. Following contamination, it computes weighted capability restrictions using binary, fractional, or fractional-flow strategies without auxiliary language-model inference. We evaluate SkillGuard on four AgentDojo suites with two backend LLMs, Gemini 2.5 Flash and Llama3.3-70B, against an LLM-only No Defense baseline and three defenses at different system layers: Spotlighting, CaMeL, and AttriGuard. We construct a compositional attack benchmark in which each attack combines observations individually insufficient to induce target violation and evaluate the same baselines on it. Under AgentDojo's Tool Knowledge attacks, SkillGuard eliminates attack success on three of four suites for both backends and reduces it to 4.8% and 14.3% on Slack. Against compositional attacks, it outperforms every baseline on Llama and matches the strongest baseline on Gemini at higher benign utility. Fractional-flow restriction preserves substantially more capabilities than binary restriction at the same attack success rate. Across both settings, SkillGuard adds no model calls or token overhead.
2608.30041.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型代理將外部技能的輸出放入其執行上下文中，允許攻擊者控制的數據影響後續的特權行動。現有的防禦主要是對不受信內容進行分類或授權提議的操作。它們並未直接解決一旦不受信數據進入其狀態後，代理的未來權限應如何改變。我們提出了SkillGuard，一個在執行層級的強制執行層，將此事件視為污染，並限制未來的能力，以斷開結果狀態與部署者定義的禁止狀態之間的聯繫。在給定的可靠技能摘要和政策下，SkillGuard用技能影響圖表示與安全相關的轉換，通過可引導性簽名指定對技能參數的可接受控制，並通過內聯參考監視器調解調用。在污染之後，它使用二元、分數或分數流策略計算加權能力限制，而無需輔助的語言模型推斷。我們在四個AgentDojo套件上評估SkillGuard，使用兩個後端LLM，Gemini 2.5 Flash和Llama3.3-70B，與僅有LLM的無防禦基線和三個不同系統層的防禦進行比較：Spotlighting、CaMeL和AttriGuard。我們構建了一個組合攻擊基準，其中每個攻擊結合了單獨不足以引發目標違規的觀察，並在其上評估相同的基線。在AgentDojo的工具知識攻擊下，SkillGuard消除了四個套件中三個的攻擊成功率，並將Slack的攻擊成功率降低到4.8%和14.3%。在對抗組合攻擊時，它在Llama上超越了每個基線，並在Gemini上以更高的良性效用匹配最強的基線。在相同的攻擊成功率下，分數流限制保留的能力顯著多於二元限制。在這兩種情況下，SkillGuard未增加任何模型調用或標記開銷。
